messages:
maya: Hey team — quick follow-up from the latency incident last night. We need to formalize the PRD changes + runbook guardrails so we don't regress. Proposing a small scoped PRD update (must/have-to-have) plus a runbook playbook and a short RFC for gating rules. Thoughts?
kevin-bot: INCIDENT: 2026-03-18 23:14 UTC - routing fallback caused ~6x latency for some customers. Auto-mitigation triggered.
alex: Agree we need tight scope. Suggest 2 artifacts: 1) PRD change to routing fallback policy and acceptance criteria, 2) runbook snippet + automation to detect and rollback bad fallback mappings.
samira: Also add an SLO guardrail and a circuit-breaker on model-variant fallback depth. Last night the chain of fallbacks cascaded. We should cap recursion and add alerting.
jon: Implementation note: capping fallback depth is straightforward config change, but the kernel-level batching optimizations that reduce p95 might be impacted if we change routing behavior. We should include perf regression acceptance tests in the PRD.
tara: Customers flagged: "AetnaHealth" and "NoteFlow" asked for explicit SLA promises about p95 latency after the outage. They want timelines. Can we give a target?
maya: Proposed must-have PRD items (short):
- Define guardrail: max fallback depth = 2
- Define circuit-breaker: open if error rate > 1% for 2 mins
- SLO target: p95 < 500ms for hosted API for standard tier under baseline load
- Rollout criterion: 72h canary with synthetic workload, no SLO regressions, and runbook steps rehearsed
- Acceptance tests: perf harness run + smoke tests for KV cache correctness
Please comment on feasibility and scope.
alex: Feasibility: can deliver config + runbook changes in ~3 business days for canary, maybe 7 for full rollout depending on QA cycles. We need to drop anything that requires kernel changes from the must-have list (move to should-have).
jon: +1. Kernel patches are higher risk — propose we put kernel perf changes into the Optimize backlog as a follow-up. For this PRD, include a "no kernel change" constraint unless signoff from runtime eng and SRE.
samira: Runbook addition suggestion (draft snippet):
```
- Detect: p95 > 500ms OR fallback_count > 2 for 5m -> fire "fallback-latency" alert
- Mitigate: switch traffic to primary variants in region A using routing policy 'prefer-primary'
- If mitigation fails: escalate to oncall, run 'revert-routing' script, open BCP ticket
- Postmortem: add events to incident log and attach perf traces
```
We can autom8 the first two steps.
tara: For customer comms: we need an "expected window" to promise. If canary finishes in 72h we can say ETA 2 weeks for full rollout. They want that in writing.
maya: Good. I'll put "2 weeks ETA for full rollout pending canary" in the PRD timeline.
jon: Edge cases to call out in PRD:
- Traffic spikes that change model-dominant routing distribution -> verify batch sizes don't regress p50/p95 badly
- Cold KV cache after canary swap -> validate cache-warmup plan
- Region-by-region rollout differences (some regions have different latency baselines)
We should include acceptance criteria per-region.
alex: Scope negotiation: Must-haves = guardrail config, runbook + automation for detection+mitigation, canary plan, acceptance tests. Should-haves = kernel batching changes, per-customer QoS controls (this can be an expedited follow-up if sales pushes).
maya: I'll draft PRD with those sections and add a short RFC for "routing-gate" rules that will be reviewed by eng-runtime and SRE. Who wants to be review owners?
samira: SRE review owner: samira. I'll take the runbook + alert thresholds.
jon: Runtime review: jon. I'll add the perf test templates to the PRD.
tara: CS owner: tara — I'll coordinate customer comms and track AetnaHealth / NoteFlow expectations.
alex: Platform owner: alex — I'll own the canary plan and rollout automation.
maya: Great. Action items:
- maya: PRD draft v0 with must/should lists and timeline (due EOD tomorrow)
- samira: runbook + alert thresholds (due +2 days)
- jon: perf acceptance tests + no-kernel-change constraint language (due +3 days)
- alex: canary plan + rollback scripts (due +3 days)
- tara: customer comms template (due +1 day)
Please react with :thumbsup: if you agree to the owners.
samira: :thumbsup:
jon: :thumbsup:
alex: :thumbsup:
tara: :thumbsup:
maya: Thanks all. Quick follow-up: add an "expedited path" section in PRD for high-value customers that may request per-customer QoS. We'll set clear cost/engineering tradeoffs.
jon: One more technical acceptance criterion: add end-to-end trace sampling for fallback routing steps so we can quickly triage later.
maya: noted. I'll add trace sampling and attach a sample trace format in the PRD.
kevin-bot: REMINDER: post-incident RFC required for compliance. Please attach incident timeline + mitigations to PRD.
maya: Will do. I'll upload initial PRD draft to the product docs space and ping reviewers. Expect link in this thread by EOD tomorrow.
alex: If anyone hits blockers on rollback automation, ping me directly. We can scope a temporary routing-policy toggle until full automation lands.
tara: I'll update the customers with "we're targeting 2 weeks for full rollout after a 72h canary; we'll share the PRD tomorrow". They asked for weekly status updates until rollout.
maya: Closing notes: keep the PRD tight, minimal scope for safety, move larger perf work into Optimize backlog. Thanks everyone.
